recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is +17.5% above baseline (92.0 ms latest, 78.4 ms recent avg) — strong recovery signal
Resting HR is -5.5% below baseline (47.6 bpm), consistent with parasympathetic dominance
ACWR = 0.7 — low, indicating detraining risk if sustained, but currently reflects reduced load, not fatigue
Sleep remains chronically insufficient: 5.2 h avg (14/14 nights <7h), undermining HRV sustainability
Recovery balance = +4.96 (well above 0), but driven more by low acute load than robust recovery capacity
readiness.guidance: You’re physiologically recovered *today*, but chronic sleep debt and low training load mean this isn’t sustainable readiness — prioritize sleep consistency before increasing volume or intensity.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows markedly reduced volume and intensity versus last month, with slower average pace and lower zone 3–4 time, but improved aerobic efficiency and stable VO₂max — a deliberate taper or unintentional de-load.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +32 spm month-over-month — the largest absolute change in any metric — and aligns with a sharp drop in ground contact time (298–301 ms recently vs 370 ms on 2026-07-31), suggesting a conscious or adaptive shift toward quicker turnover, likely compensating for reduced fitness stimulus.

goal_tracker.message: You need 34.1 km across 5 remaining sessions — ~6.8 km/session — to match last month’s volume. However, given chronic sleep debt (<7h for all 14 days) and ACWR of 0.7 (low, not optimal), chasing this number would reinforce under-recovery and delay aerobic development. Prioritize sleep hygiene and one easy zone 2 run over hitting the km target.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated Running Economy
insights.body: Despite HRV rebound, running economy has worsened (13.98 vs 13.64) while sleep averaged only 5.2 h (14/14 nights <7h); poor sleep impairs neuromuscular coordination and metabolic efficiency — reflected in higher ml O2/kg/km and increased vertical oscillation (7.5–8.0 cm recently vs 6.6 cm on easy runs).

insights.title: Low acute load masks aerobic fragility
insights.body: Aerobic decoupling median is 7.11% (above 5% threshold), yet latest reading is 4.8% — the improvement coincides with lowest weekly TRIMP in 4 weeks (101), suggesting decoupling worsens when load increases, not that it’s resolved. The 9.37% decoupling on 2026-08-02 (2.7 km, HR 119) hints at inefficient effort distribution even at low intensity.

insights.title: Cadence surge lacks stride length support
insights.body: Cadence rose +32 spm MoM (150 vs 118), but stride length dropped from 74.88 cm (2026-08-05) to 65.7 cm (2026-08-23) — a 12% reduction — and ground contact time increased from 283 ms to 385 ms on the slowest run. This suggests compensatory short-stepping rather than efficient neuromuscular adaptation.

insights.title: VO₂max improved (+4.8%) despite low load — proof of recovery quality
insights.body: VO₂max rose from baseline 37.4 to 40.0 (+1.8 avg, +4.8% vs baseline) while acute load fell 41% below baseline and ACWR dropped to 0.7 — confirming that high-quality recovery (HRV +17.5%, resting HR -5.5%) can drive aerobic gains even without high volume.

recommendations.action: Prioritize sleep: aim for ≥7 hours on 4 of the next 6 nights — use Body Battery as a proxy; avoid screens after 21:00 and keep bedroom temp ≤23°C.
recommendations.reason: 14/14 nights <7h sleep directly undermines running economy, decoupling resilience, and long-term HRV sustainability — no training stimulus will compound without this foundation.

recommendations.action: One 45-min Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, pace ~5:30–6:00/km) on Tuesday — no distance target, just time-in-zone and cadence focus (152–156 spm, using metronome).
recommendations.reason: Maintains aerobic stimulus without adding load stress; aligns with current readiness (ACWR 0.7, recovery balance +4.96) and counters recent cadence-stride disconnect.

recommendations.action: Two 10-min post-run mobility sessions (hip flexor + calf releases + diaphragmatic breathing) on Thursday and Saturday.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation increased to 7.5–8.0 cm (vs 6.6 cm on easiest run) and ground contact time spiked to 385 ms on 2026-08-23 — signs of stiffness and inefficient force transfer needing direct intervention.

risk_flags.evidence: 14/14 nights <7h sleep in last 14 days, HRV trending upward but not yet resilient enough to offset neural fatigue
risk_flags.action: Implement strict sleep window (22:30–05:30) for next 7 days; track with Garmin Sleep Score — target ≥85.

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence up +32 spm but stride length down 12% and ground contact time up 35 ms on slowest run (385 ms), vertical oscillation up to 8.0 cm
risk_flags.action: Pause cadence-focused drills until stride length stabilizes ≥72 cm at easy pace; add 2x/week single-leg glute bridges.

weekly_focus.description: Stabilize sleep architecture and neuromuscular coordination before reintroducing load — prioritize consistency of rest, rhythm, and range over pace or distance.
suggested_sessions: Very light active recovery (e.g., 20-min walk + foam roll)
